headline: Central Valley lawmakers weigh in on mental health diversion bills as they pass key guardrail
content:
The Daily Brief

Central Valley lawmakers weigh in on mental health diversion bills as they pass key guardrail

Good morning, Bakersfield. We're starting off warm with a high near 95° and air quality at a moderate 52. Overnight, a welfare check involving a red pickup at Chester and Belle Terrace kept law enforcement busy, and today's top story looks at Kern County's role in shaping a national addiction toolkit for the homeless. Pour some coffee and let's catch up on the valley.

The Kern Overnight

A busy night unfolded across Kern County, with law enforcement handling most of the action. Around 11:34 p.m., Bakersfield police broadcast an urgent attempt-to-locate and welfare check after a caller reported a red pickup at South Chester Avenue and Belle Terrace. The caller described a male hanging out the driver's window while a female cried for help. The truck was last seen heading southbound, prompting a citywide alert for any unit to locate it. Earlier in the evening, around 9:23 p.m., city units responded to White Lane for a road-rage disturbance involving a blue Honda with paper plates and a white pickup, both repeatedly stopping and blocking eastbound traffic. At 10:33 p.m., a white 2001 Dodge van with California plates was reported stolen on Kentucky Street, with officers taking the report on scene. Just before midnight, CHP broadcast a DUI on southbound I-5 south of the Grapevine after a newer black pickup was seen speeding over 90 mph and passing on the shoulder while the driver drank from an open container. Fire crews had a quieter night, responding to a residential alarm on Greenview Lane around 11 p.m. that turned out to be nothing, and a vehicle accident drawing an engine, battalion, and rescue unit to a county location. The night also saw a theft reported from a mobile home park on Barlow Road, with a loss estimated near $3,900 and a suspect named from within the same park.

Today's weather

Today's forecast calls for a high near 95° and a low around 67° tonight. It's currently 88° at Meadows Field (KBFL), and we're looking at mostly sunny skies with no active weather alerts for Kern County. Air quality is moderate at an AQI of 52, so it's a good day to keep windows open and enjoy the breeze.

Top stories

KGET 17 reports that Kern County is playing a key role in shaping a national addiction toolkit aimed at helping the homeless community. Carlos Baldovinos, executive director of the Mission at Kern County, recently traveled to San Diego for the public release of the federal best practices guide, which he helped develop alongside roughly 22 professionals from across the country. The toolkit outlines best practices for working with individuals dealing with addiction within the homeless population, covering topics such as program length, transitional housing, long-term mentorship, and workforce development. Baldovinos emphasized the importance of long-term recovery programs, pushing back against the notion that addiction treatment should be limited to short-term interventions like 28-day programs.

23ABC shares that Kern County supervisors are exploring a proposal that would place Kern and dozens of other counties in a new state, separate from coastal California. Kern County District 3 Supervisor Jeff Flores says the effort is about ensuring the region's industries and way of life are taken seriously by state leaders. An analysis presented to the board found the proposed inland state would account for only about 15 percent of California's current real GDP, with CSU Bakersfield economics professor Richard Gearhart noting that separation would drop California from the fourth-largest economy in the world to roughly the 16th-largest state economy in the country—comparable to Missouri. Gearhart warns that the proposed inland state would lose significant economic opportunities and growth by cutting itself off from a highly educated workforce and thriving industries.

Something good

The Kern County Fair has announced its Grandstand Arena events, offering a variety of entertainment options for the community to enjoy. From live music to family-friendly activities, the fair promises to bring plenty of excitement and fun to the valley.

Coming up this week

Looking ahead, there are several public meetings and events worth noting. On Tuesday, August 18, the Multi Modal Transportation and Traffic Safety Committee meets at 12:00 p.m., followed by the Historic Preservation Commission at 4:00 p.m. and the Miscellaneous Civil Service Commission at 2:00 p.m. On Wednesday, August 19, the Water Board convenes at 10:00 a.m. Additionally, the Planning Commission will meet on Thursday, August 20, at 5:30 p.m. For entertainment, the Fox Theater has a packed lineup: PEPPER with CYDEWAYS takes the stage tonight, August 14; Los Yonic's Zamacona, Los caminantes, y Grupo Yndio perform on August 22; Rodney Carrington brings his show on August 27; CUMBIATRON: THE CUMBIA RAVE happens on August 28; and Willie Barcena and Michael Return Of The King Tribute Featuring Michael Phoenix both perform on August 29. Be sure to check the Fox Theater's website for tickets and details.
